title: National Commission's Authority to Investigate Allegations

content.scenario: A complaint is filed against the President of a State Commission, alleging misconduct. The National Commission initiates an investigation and submits an inquiry report to the State Government.
content.outcome: The National Commission has the authority to investigate allegations against the President and members of a State Commission and submit an inquiry report to the State Government concerned, along with a copy endorsed to the Central Government for necessary action, as per Section 70(1)(b) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What is the National Commission's role in investigating allegations against State Commission members?
Can the National Commission submit an inquiry report to the State Government?
What action can the Central Government take based on the inquiry report?
